plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 after material_data failure with Si/SiO2 system. Previous iteration produced zero physically valid candidates due to material import issues in the mid-IR range. Three new routes proposed: (1) switch to Ge/ZnS material pair with documented mid-IR transparency, (2) alternative ZnSe/ZnS pair for lower absorption, (3) reduced 20-layer topology to improve manufacturability. All routes preserve the dual-cavity dual-band scientific principle while making concrete material and topology changes. Each route has explicit layer count, fixed topology, and thickness bounds [100, 500] nm to guarantee solver feasibility.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Dual-Cavity Dual-Band Bandpass Filter on CaF2
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Germanium (high-index) and Zinc Sulfide (low-index) form a viable material pair for mid-IR dual-band bandpass filters on CaF2 substrate, achieving high transmission in 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm bands while blocking 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm, with 22 total layers in a dual-cavity topology.
routes.design_principle: Dual-cavity bandpass filter constructed from alternating high/low index quarter-wave stacks, with two resonance cavities tuned to methane and CO2 absorption bands respectively. Ge provides high index contrast (~4.0 vs ~2.3) for sharp spectral edges.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | Ge cavity | [Ge/ZnS]_3 | ZnS cavity | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | CaF2 substrate. Total 22 finite layers: 5+5=10 mirror layers, 3+3=6 mirror layers, 2 cavity layers, plus 4 transition layers = 22 layers exact.
design_variables: Cavity layer positions fixed at layers 11 and 17
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional PVD-depositable IR materials
Thickness bounds [100, 500] nm ensure deposition feasibility
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack principle for bandpass filters
Ge/ZnS index contrast suitable for mid-IR
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS pair has documented mid-IR transparency unlike Si/SiO2
Higher index contrast than Si/SiO2 enables sharper band edges
22 layers provides sufficient blocking while staying under 24-layer limit
known_risks: Ge may exhibit absorption features in mid-IR requiring verification
Thermal stress between Ge and ZnS during deposition
Cavity coupling may produce unwanted spectral ripple
routes.execution_request_english: Using Transfer Matrix Method, optimize a 22-layer dielectric stack on CaF2 substrate with air incidence at normal angle. Layer sequence: Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS, Ge, ZnS. Initialize all thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness at 3300 nm center wavelength. Set thickness optimization bounds [100, 500] nm for all layers. Evaluate transmittance across four bands: 2500-3100 nm (suppress), 3250-3350 nm (transmit), 4200-4300 nm (transmit), 4450-5000 nm (suppress). Use Ge and ZnS as dielectric materials with CaF2 substrate. No metal layers allowed. Total layer count fixed at 22. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Changed material system from Si/SiO2 to Ge/ZnS to address material_data failure. Si/SiO2 has absorption issues in mid-IR range; Ge/ZnS is documented for mid-IR bandpass applications. Preserved dual-cavity topology and 22-layer count from route_02.

routes.title: ZnSe/ZnS Dual-Cavity Dual-Band Bandpass Filter on CaF2
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Zinc Selenide (high-index) and Zinc Sulfide (low-index) form a lower-absorption alternative material pair for mid-IR dual-band bandpass filters, achieving comparable performance to Ge/ZnS with reduced thermal stress and better mid-IR transparency.
routes.design_principle: Same dual-cavity topology as route_02 but with ZnSe/ZnS material pair. ZnSe has lower absorption coefficient than Ge in 3-5 μm range while maintaining adequate index contrast (~2.4 vs ~2.3).
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [ZnSe/ZnS]_5 | ZnSe cavity | [ZnSe/ZnS]_3 | ZnS cavity | [ZnSe/ZnS]_5 | CaF2 substrate. Total 22 finite layers exact.
design_variables: Cavity layer positions fixed at layers 11 and 17
manufacturing_considerations: ZnSe and ZnS are both conventional PVD-depositable IR materials
Lower thermal stress than Ge/ZnS due to matched thermal expansion
Thickness bounds [100, 500] nm ensure deposition feasibility
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack principle for bandpass filters
ZnSe/ZnS lower absorption in mid-IR than Ge-based systems
expected_advantages: Lower material absorption than Ge/ZnS in 3-5 μm range
Both materials well-documented for IR coating applications
known_risks: Lower index contrast than Ge/ZnS may require more layers for equivalent blocking
ZnSe is more expensive than Ge
May not achieve same band edge sharpness as Ge/ZnS

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Reduced-Layer Dual-Cavity Filter on CaF2
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing total layer count from 22 to 20 while maintaining dual-cavity topology improves manufacturability and reduces cumulative thickness error, with acceptable trade-off in out-of-band blocking performance for this satellite application.
routes.design_principle: Same Ge/ZnS material pair as route_02_refine_01 but with reduced mirror pair count. 20 layers reduces deposition time and cumulative thickness error while maintaining dual-cavity resonance structure.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/ZnS]_4 | Ge cavity | [Ge/ZnS]_3 | ZnS cavity | [Ge/ZnS]_4 | CaF2 substrate. Total 20 finite layers exact: 4+4=8 mirror layers, 3+3=6 mirror layers, 2 cavity layers, plus 4 transition layers = 20 layers.
design_variables: Cavity layer positions fixed at layers 9 and 15
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count 20 ≤ 24 constraint satisfied with margin
Reduced layer count improves deposition yield
theory_basis: Dual-cavity resonance with reduced mirror pairs
Trade-off between layer count and blocking performance
known_risks: Reduced out-of-band blocking compared to 22-layer design
May not meet suppression requirements in 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm bands
Steeper spectral edges may be compromised

Trade-off between 20-layer manufacturability and 22-layer blocking performance requires experimental validation
Cavity coupling strength and spectral ripple amplitude not predictable without TMM simulation results
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
